data.name: Mitochondrial biogenesis
data.description: Production of new mitochondria and their oxidative machinery. mTORC1 drives it via a YY1-PGC-1alpha transcriptional program, linking growth signaling to energy production.
data.description_beginner: Building new mitochondria - a cell's power plants. mTORC1 drives this process through a genetic program, linking growth signals directly to how much energy-making machinery a cell has.

studies.title: mTOR controls mitochondrial oxidative function through a YY1-PGC-1alpha transcriptional complex
studies.authors: Cunningham JT; Rodgers JT; Arlow DH; Vazquez F; Mootha VK; Puigserver P

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Showed mTOR isn't just about building proteins - it also runs the cell's POWER plants. mTORC1 drives mitochondrial gene expression and oxygen consumption through a YY1-PGC-1alpha transcriptional program; block mTOR with rapamycin and mitochondrial output falls. Explains part of why mTOR inhibition reshapes metabolism.

studies.title: Skeletal muscle-specific ablation of raptor, but not of rictor, causes metabolic changes and results in muscle dystrophy
studies.authors: Bentzinger CF; Rueegg MA et al.

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: In mice, muscle-specific raptor loss (not rictor) causes dystrophy, showing mTORC1 is essential for muscle homeostasis.

studies.title: Nutrient/TOR signaling controls adipose mitochondrial transcription factor A (TFAM) to regulate organismal growth in Drosophila

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: In Drosophila larvae, nutrient/TOR signaling in the fat body (a key nutrient-sensing tissue) post-transcriptionally suppresses the mitochondrial transcription factor TFAM, and this TOR→TFAM axis in fat-body tissue controls whole-body developmental growth — a mechanistic link between nutrient sensing and interorgan growth control via mitochondrial bioenergetics.

relations.mechanism: In mammalian cells (MOR2013) 4E-BPs repress translation of nucleus-encoded mitochondrial mRNAs, so mTORC1 raises mitochondrial output by inhibiting them; this arm is less rapamycin-sensitive than the S6K arm. In flies on dietary restriction (ZID2009) upregulated 4E-BP instead enhances translation of mitochondrial respiratory mRNAs. The sign depends on organism and nutrient state, so it is drawn as conditional.
relations.mechanism_beginner: The 4E-BP branch helps set how many mitochondrial proteins get built. In mammalian cells it holds them back; in fruit flies on a restricted diet it boosts them, so the direction depends on the organism and the diet.
relations.boundary: Scope: mammalian cells, MOR2013. The sign holds where 4E-BP represses translation of nuclear-encoded mitochondrial mRNAs (TFAM, mitochondrial ribosomal proteins), which is why this branch survives rapamycin better than the S6K arm. It does NOT hold universally across species and nutrient states: in Drosophila under dietary restriction, ZID2009 reports that 4E-BP ENHANCES mitochondrial activity, and that this is how it extends lifespan. Treat the mammalian-cell direction as scoped, not general.
relations.note: ZID2009 is recorded as conflicting evidence on this edge (moved out of the supporting list on 2026-08-30): its own title says 4E-BP ENHANCES mitochondrial activity under dietary restriction in flies, which is the opposite sign to this mammalian-cell edge.

relations.mechanism: mTORC1 raises mitochondrial output two ways: through a YY1-PGC-1alpha transcription complex, and by relieving 4E-BP so mitochondrial proteins get translated.
relations.mechanism_beginner: mTORC1 boosts the cell's mitochondria – its power plants – two ways at once: through a gene-activating complex, and by freeing up 4E-BP.
relations.boundary: Shown in cultured cells and skeletal muscle (CUN2007) and mammalian cell lines (MOR2013). One organismal result points the other way: adipose-specific Raptor deletion raised mitochondrial respiration (POL2008), see MTORC1-OXPHOS.
